reasoning_traces.think:
The framework begins with temporal segmentation of player-tracking data into actions, defined as continuous periods satisfying specific criteria such as presence of dribbling and proximity constraints. Each action is then mapped to a 150-dimensional feature vector derived from pairwise distances between players and the basket. These features are discretized into binary quintiles to reduce dimensionality while preserving discriminative power. A machine learning classifier trained on this dataset distinguishes on-ball screens from non-screens. The system's robustness hinges on accurate labeling and sufficient representation of diverse teams and scenarios. Failure modes include misclassification due to noisy data or insufficient training samples, particularly in edge cases like handoffs or complex defensive rotations.
